title: Visa’s “every utterance is a game invite” doctrine
summary:
visakanv basically drops a cheat code for the internet in 2018—“every utterance… is a proposal… ‘let’s play this game’”—and then spends the next six years watching people use it to stop getting into pointless fights and start making actual friends. The original trigger is Visa ranting that most people can’t reply worth a damn: you’re supposed to *support the OP’s game* (even when disagreeing), not just “speak your mind.” His big claim is brutally practical: read the implicit bid correctly, respond in a way that shows you *got it*, and “a shared understanding develops. You can make friends this way.”

The arc goes: [trigger: Visa’s 2018 “utterances are proposals” tweet + “optimize for making friends”] → [peak: other accounts independently reinventing / synthesizing it into improv/status-game language] → [outcome: it turns into a portable framework people apply to dating, autism/status intuition, and even workshop facilitation]. goblinodds has the parallel epiphany via Keith Johnstone—“conversations are supposed to be fun,” “the point is PLAY”—then ties it to status theory (“acquaintances become friends when they agree to play status games together,” and autistic difficulty as missing *intuitive* status sense). forthrighter takes Visa’s bid-reading idea and makes it explicit: every conversation has two tracks (“relationship/group building” vs “what we’re talking about”), and the “devil’s advocate” move often accidentally reads as a rejected bid. Then nosilverv detonates the viral synthesis in 2022: “everything is improv theatre… every utterance is an invitation,” and if you treat it like info-exchange you’re committing a “type error.” He even drags in PUA routines as “overwrought explanations” of the same thing: social interaction is co-creating games.

What’s left behind is a whole shared vocabulary people keep reusing: “good reply game,” “every utterance is a proposal,” “friendship is shared understanding,” and the idea that you should *choose which games you accept*. By 2023 Visa turns it into concrete tactics (“don’t DM, live in the replies; be specific; demonstrate shared understanding”), while RichDecibels ports it offline into facilitation: convening + hosting + “social process” = deliberately choosing the games that create trust/belonging (with the obligatory warning about “accelerated intimacy” being cult-adjacent if the hosts suck). If you care about internet sanity—or you just want to stop bouncing off people and start building rapport—this strand is basically: stop arguing about the object-level, start noticing what game you’re being invited to play, and respond like you actually want to be there.
